372figma_export_videofigmawritecreativeTurn code into editable design Export a Figma timeline node as an MP4 video. This tool only produces MP4 — GIF and animated SVG export are not supported yet. Renders the timeline server-side and returns a presigned download URL. The file stays available for `ttlSeconds` (defaults to 1 hour, clamped server-side to [30s, 7d]); use `availableUntil` in the response to know when it is deleted. Some renders finish in seconds, others take minutes; if the render hasn't finished within the handler budget, the response includes a `jobId` and `status: "processing"` — re-invoke `export_video` with `{ fileKey, jobId }` after 10–15s to poll. Required: `fileKey` and either `nodeId` (to start a new export) or `jobId` (to poll). The `nodeId` must be the top-level frame that owns the timeline — in a design file a frame placed directly on the page or in a section, and in Slides the slide itself (not a layer inside it) — not a nested layer or sub-clip. If you animated a descendant, pass its containing top-level frame (the slide, in Slides); if `get_motion_context` returns a `timelineCohorts` entry, its `rootNodeId` is that frame. Use the `quality` field ("low"/"medium"/"high") to control output size. This tool is part of plugin `Figma`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__figma_export_video(args: { // Output-size constraint. SCALE multiplies the node's natural size (value is the multiplier, e.g. 2 = 2x); WIDTH / HEIGHT pin that dimension to an absolute pixel count and scale the other to preserve aspect ratio. Optional; omit to render at the node's natural size (1x). Clamped server-side to a max 10x scale / 4096px per dimension. Ignored when polling with jobId. constraint?: { type: "SCALE" | "WIDTH" | "HEIGHT"; value: number; }; // The key of the Figma file to use. If the URL is provided, extract the file key from the URL. The given URL must be in the format https://figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:int1-:int2. The extracted fileKey would be `:fileKey`. fileKey: string; // Frames per second for the rendered MP4 (5-60). Optional; the server picks a default. fps?: number; // Returned from a previous call when the export was still rendering. Pass this to poll. Provide nodeId OR jobId, never both — the call is rejected if both are set. When polling, fps/quality/ttlSeconds are ignored (they were fixed when the job was created). jobId?: string; // The timeline node to export. Required when starting a new export. Provide nodeId OR jobId, never both — the call is rejected if both are set. Must be the top-level frame that owns the timeline — in a design file a frame placed directly on the page or in a section, and in Slides the slide itself (not a layer inside it) — not a nested layer or sub-clip. If you animated a descendant, pass its containing top-level frame (the slide, in Slides); if get_motion_context returns a `timelineCohorts` entry, its `rootNodeId` is that frame. nodeId?: string; // Render quality preset. Higher quality means a larger file. Optional; the server picks a default. quality?: "low" | "medium" | "high"; // How long (in seconds) the rendered MP4 is retained on the server. Each poll reissues a fresh presigned download URL; once this window elapses the file is deleted and the job is no longer reachable. Clamped server-side to [30, 7d]. ttlSeconds?: number; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; }; ```

For web apps, run both in parallel — generate_figma_design captures a pixel-perfect screenshot, use_figma builds from imported design system components and refines against the screenshot - Non-web (iOS, Android, generic UI) and from-scratch designs: use_figma only - Updating/syncing a Figma page already captured: use_figma — even if source code changed GOTCHAS - For the font "Inter", the style is "Semi Bold", not "SemiBold" and "Extra Bold" not "ExtraBold" - MUST use `await figma.setCurrentPageAsync(page)` to change pages. 396figma_weave_get_tool_inputsfigmawritecreativeTurn code into editable design Gets the input contract of a Weave tool (a published Weave workflow) — the inputs you fill in to run it. Pass the `recipeId` (from weave_list_tools, or the `<id>` in a pasted Weave URL like app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id> — that `<id>` is the recipeId). A pasted Weave URL is enough to inspect and run the tool right here — do not open a browser or use browser automation for Weave. Call this before weave_run_tool to learn what to send. Returns the tool `version` (pass it back to weave_run_tool), an `outputs` summary (what the tool produces), and a flat `inputs` list. Each input has a `nodeId` (the key you send in weave_run_tool), `name`, `type` (text, integer, boolean, select, seed, image, video, audio, 3D, color, or any), `default` (its current value), and `required` (true only when there is no current value, so you must provide one), plus `options` (for `select`), `range`, `isIterator`, and `description`. This tool is part of plugin `Figma`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__figma_weave_get_tool_inputs(args: { // The id of the Weave tool whose input contract to fetch — from weave_list_tools, or the `<id>` in a pasted Weave URL (app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id>), which is the recipeId. recipeId: string; // Tool version to inspect; omit for the latest. version?: number; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; }; ```
397figma_weave_get_tool_run_outputfigmawritecreativeTurn code into editable design Gets the output and status of runs of a Weave tool (a published Weave workflow). Pass the `recipeId` of the tool and the `runIds` returned by weave_run_tool; omit `runIds` to get the tool's most recent run. Returns each run's status (RUNNING, COMPLETED, FAILED, or CANCELED), progress, any error, and — when complete — a link to every output the run produced. Poll this after running a tool to track progress and read its output. Each output is a JSON entry with a `url`, its `type` (e.g. image, video), and, when known, `width`/`height`/`format`. The response also includes curl instructions for downloading the outputs — the URL+curl path is strongly preferred because it uses far fewer tokens than embedding media inline. This tool is part of plugin `Figma`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__figma_weave_get_tool_run_output(args: { // The id of the Weave tool whose runs to fetch (from weave_list_tools). recipeId: string; // The run ids to fetch output for, as returned by weave_run_tool. 399figma_weave_run_toolfigmadestructivecreativeTurn code into editable design Runs a Weave tool (a published Weave workflow) and returns run ids; poll them with weave_get_tool_run_output. A pasted Weave URL (app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id>) is enough — never open a browser or use browser automation for Weave. Call weave_get_tool_inputs first to learn the inputs. This tool spends the user's Weave credits, so it is gated: it returns `status: "inputs_required"` or `cost_confirmation_required` with instructions to follow. Always show the user the cost and get an explicit Approve/Cancel (a structured prompt, not free text) before echoing `acknowledgedCost` to run — every run, including reruns — and confirm any auto-filled inputs (values you did not set that the run will use). Include the response's `costDisclosure` string as its own sentence after the question, not folded into it, the first time you quote a cost in a conversation; omit it after that. For an image/video input, pass a reachable https URL directly; only upload a local file with weave_upload_asset and pass the asset object it returns. If the user wants an input you did not get from weave_get_tool_inputs, do not omit it or fold it into another input like the prompt — re-fetch weave_get_tool_inputs (its inputs can change) and set it. This tool is part of plugin `Figma`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__figma_weave_run_tool(args: { // The credit `cost` the tool quoted in its `cost_confirmation_required` response, echoed back after the user approves to confirm the spend and run. For a dynamic-cost tool (the response had `isDynamicCost: true` and `cost: null`), pass `-1` to confirm a variable charge. acknowledgedCost?: number; // Values for the inputs you want to set. Omit an input to keep its current value. inputs?: Array<{ // The input's `nodeId` from weave_get_tool_inputs. nodeId: string; value?: unknown; }>; // How many times to run the tool (1–10). numberOfRuns?: number; // The id of the Weave tool to run — from weave_list_tools, or the `<id>` in a pasted Weave URL (app.weavy.ai/tool/<id> or app.weavy.ai/flow/<id>), which is the recipeId. recipeId: string; // The tool `version` from weave_get_tool_inputs; omit to run the latest. version?: number; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; }; ```
400figma_weave_upload_assetfigmasensitive-writecreativeTurn code into editable design Uploads a local image or video file to Weave and returns the asset object to pass as the value for an image/video input in weave_run_tool. Returns a `submitUrl` and a `token`: POST the file to the submitUrl as multipart/form-data with a `file` field and the token in an `X-Weave-Upload-Token` header (e.g. `curl -F "file=@/path/to/image.png" -H "X-Weave-Upload-Token: <token>" "<submitUrl>"`); that POST returns the asset object. If you already have a reachable https URL, do not upload it — pass it directly to weave_run_tool. If the media exists only in this conversation (you have no path or URL for it), ask the user to save it and give you a path or URL. The token expires in about 10 minutes. This tool is part of plugin `Figma`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__figma_weave_upload_asset(args: { [key: string]: unknown; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; }; ```

424gamma_export_gammagammadestructivecreativeCreate presentations and docs Starts exporting an existing Gamma presentation or document to a downloadable file. Use this when the user wants a PDF, PowerPoint (pptx), or PNG image export of a Gamma they already have. Requires the Gamma file ID or URL and the format: "pdf", "pptx", or "png" (png returns a ZIP archive with one PNG per card). This returns an exportId immediately. Where an interactive widget is displayed, it shows export progress and the download link on its own, so do not call get_export_status. Where there is no interactive widget, such as a CLI or terminal client that does not render MCP Apps, poll get_export_status with the exportId, waiting a few seconds between checks (do not tight-loop), until the status is "completed" or "failed". On completion, share the download URL; on failure, report the error or reason. Do NOT call export_gamma again to check progress (that starts a brand-new export). The download link expires after about one week and is not tied to the API key, so share it carefully and download promptly. This tool is part of plugin `Gamma`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gamma_export_gamma(args: { // Output format: "pdf" → a .pdf, "pptx" → a .pptx, "png" → a .zip archive containing one PNG per card (not a single image). exportAs: "pdf" | "pptx" | "png"; // The Gamma file ID or a full Gamma URL to export. The generationId or /generations/ URL returned by a generate tool is also accepted and automatically resolves once generation completes. Examples: "g5aykcic8ujm71s" or "https://gamma.app/docs/My-Deck-g5aykcic8ujm71s". gammaIdOrUrl: string; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; }; ```
425gamma_generategammasensitive-writecreativeCreate presentations and docs Use this when the user wants to create a NEW presentation, document, webpage, or social media post. Use generate for any creation request unless the user references a template they want to create from. This tool can only create new content — it cannot edit, modify, or refine an existing Gamma (including one it previously generated). After generation, direct the user to open their Gamma via the gammaUrl to make any edits, theme changes, or refinements in the Gamma editor. Do not offer to adjust, tweak, or refine the generated content yourself. Only include optional parameters when the user explicitly requests or clearly implies them. Gamma has intelligent defaults. When in doubt, omit. When uncertain about user preferences, ask rather than assume. Always share the output gammaUrl with the user when it's available. This tool is part of plugin `Gamma`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gamma_generate(args: { additionalInstructions?: string; cardOptions?: { dimensions?: "16x9" | "4x3" | "fluid" | "letter" | "a4" | "pageless" | "1x1" | "4x5" | "9x16"; headerFooter?: { bottomCenter?: unknown; bottomLeft?: unknown; bottomRight?: unknown; hideFromFirstCard?: boolean; hideFromLastCard?: boolean; topCenter?: unknown; topLeft?: { size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"; source?: "themeLogo" | "custom"; src?: string; type: "cardNumber" | "image" | "text"; value?: string; }; topRight?: unknown; }; }; cardSplit?: "inputTextBreaks" | "auto"; exportAs?: "pptx" | "pdf" | "png"; folderIds?: Array<string>; format?: "presentation" | "document" | "social" | "webpage"; imageOptions?: { model?: "dall-e-3" | "imagen-3-flash" | "imagen-4-pro" | "imagen-4-ultra" | "ideogram-v3" | "ideogram-v3-turbo" | "ideogram-v3-quality" | "flux-kontext-pro" | "flux-kontext-fast" | "leonardo-phoenix" | "recraft-v3" | "recraft-v3-svg" | "recraft-v4" | "recraft-v4-svg" | "recraft-v4-pro" | "luma-photon-1" | "luma-photon-flash-1" | "gpt-image-1-medium" | "gpt-image-1-high" | "gemini-2.5-flash-image" | "gemini-3-pro-image" | "gemini-3-pro-image-hd" | "gemini-3.1-flash-image-mini" | "gemini-3.1-flash-image" | "gemini-3.1-flash-image-hd" | "flux-2-pro" | "flux-2-flex" | "flux-2-max" | "flux-2-klein"; source?: "aiGenerated" | "webAllImages" | "webFreeToUse" | "webFreeToUseCommercially" | "pictographic" | "giphy" | "pexels" | "placeholder" | "noImages" | "themeAccent"; style?: string; stylePreset?: "photorealistic" | "illustration" | "abstract" | "3D" | "lineArt" | "custom"; }; inputText: string; numCards?: number; sharingOptions?: { emailOptions?: { access: "edit" | "comment" | "view" | "fullAccess"; recipients: Array<string>; }; externalAccess?: "edit" | "comment" | "view" | "noAccess"; workspaceAccess?: "edit" | "comment" | "view" | "noAccess" | "fullAccess"; }; textMode?: "generate" | "condense" | "preserve"; textOptions?: { amount?: "brief" | "medium" | "detailed" | "extensive"; audience?: string; language?: "en" | "en-gb" | "en-in" | "es" | "es-es" | "es-mx" | "es-419" | "ca" | "fr" | "zh-cn" | "zh-tw" | "ko" | "ja" | "ja-da" | "pt-br" | "pt-pt" | "de" | "it" | "ru" | "pl" | "uk" | "ro" | "hu" | "cs" | "el" | "tr" | "ar" | "ar-sa" | "he" | "fa" | "nl" | "sv" | "da" | "nb" | "fi" | "id" | "vi" | "hi" | "gu" | "mr" | "te" | "bn" | "ta" | "ur" | "kn" | "ml" | "th" | "sr" | "hr" | "sq" | "bg" | "sl" | "bs" | "mk" | "sw" | "ha" | "yo" | "tl" | "ms" | "kk" | "uz" | "af" | "lv" | "lt" | "et" | "is" | "cy"; tone?: string; }; themeId?: string; title?: string; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; }; ```
426gamma_generate_from_templategammadestructivecreativeCreate presentations and docs Use this when the user wants to create a NEW gamma by adapting, remixing, or transforming an existing template gamma. The source template gamma’s structure (card count, sections, layout) is preserved by default, but the prompt can direct changes — e.g. adding/removing/reordering cards, adapting for a different audience, transforming the subject matter, replacing images, populating cards from supplied data, or substituting variables and placeholders. Unlike the generate tool (which determines structure from scratch), this tool starts from an existing template gamma and uses it as the source material for the new one. Choose this tool whenever the user references an existing template gamma as the starting point — whether they want to populate it with new content, adapt it for a different audience or topic, generate a variation, or maintain consistent styling across multiple generated gammas. Requires a gammaId identifying the source template gamma in the user’s workspace. Important: the input gammaId MUST point to a template gamma; a regular non-template gamma won't be accepted. Prefer IDs returned by get_gammas with type="template". If the user provided a template ID, you may use it as-is. Do not pass URLs, placeholder IDs, or regular/non-template gamma IDs. If this tool reports that the gamma is not accessible or is not a template, recover by calling get_gammas with type="template" to find a valid template, or use generate if the user actually wanted to create from non-template source material. This tool can only create new content — it cannot edit, modify, or refine an existing Gamma (including one it previously generated). After generation, direct the user to open their Gamma via the gammaUrl to make any edits, theme changes, or refinements in the Gamma editor. Do not offer to adjust, tweak, or refine the generated content yourself. Only include optional parameters when the user explicitly requests or clearly implies them. Gamma has intelligent defaults. When in doubt, omit. When uncertain about user preferences, ask rather than assume. Always share the output gammaUrl with the user when it's available. This tool is part of plugin `Gamma`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gamma_generate_from_template(args: { // Export format: 'pptx' (PowerPoint), 'pdf', or 'png'. Only include when the user explicitly requests an export. Note: 'png' returns a ZIP archive containing one PNG per card (not a single PNG file) — the exportUrl will point at a .zip. The returned exportUrl expires after approximately one week and is not tied to your API key — prompt the user to download promptly and treat it as a secret. exportAs?: "pptx" | "pdf" | "png"; // Array of folder IDs to organize the generated content (only include if requested by the user, get IDs from get_folders tool). Max 10. folderIds?: Array<string>; // The ID of a template gamma in the user's workspace. This must be the `id` field from a get_gammas result whose type is "template", or a user-provided template ID. Do not invent or guess this value. Do not pass URLs, placeholder IDs, or IDs for regular/non-template gammas. If you need to discover a valid template ID, call get_gammas with type="template" and pass the returned `id` field through unchanged. gammaId: string; // Advanced: Overrides for AI image generation. Only applies when the template uses AI-generated images — if the template uses another image source (Pictographic, web, Pexels, etc.), these options are ignored and the response returns a warning. Only include if the user explicitly requests specific image settings. imageOptions?: { // Only include if the user explicitly requests a specific image model. model?: "dall-e-3" | "imagen-3-flash" | "imagen-4-pro" | "imagen-4-ultra" | "ideogram-v3" | "ideogram-v3-turbo" | "ideogram-v3-quality" | "flux-kontext-pro" | "flux-kontext-fast" | "leonardo-phoenix" | "recraft-v3" | "recraft-v3-svg" | "recraft-v4" | "recraft-v4-svg" | "recraft-v4-pro" | "luma-photon-1" | "luma-photon-flash-1" | "gpt-image-1-medium" | "gpt-image-1-high" | "gemini-2.5-flash-image" | "gemini-3-pro-image" | "gemini-3-pro-image-hd" | "gemini-3.1-flash-image-mini" | "gemini-3.1-flash-image" | "gemini-3.1-flash-image-hd" | "flux-2-pro" | "flux-2-flex" | "flux-2-max" | "flux-2-klein"; // Custom art style prompt for AI images (e.g., "watercolor with soft pastels", "retro pixel art"). Max 500 characters. style?: string; }; // Text describing how to adapt, remix, or transform the source template gamma. May contain new content to apply (text, documents, data, messaging, embedded image URLs pasted inline where the image should appear), adaptation directives (e.g. “make this for a healthcare audience,” “remove the team section,” “reorder so Our Solution comes before The Problem,” “replace [[client-name]] with Acme Corp”), or a mix of both. When the user has supplied new content or source data (a document, data table, new messaging, image URLs), include it verbatim — do not summarize. When the intent is an adaptation directive, keep the prompt concise. Budget note: the prompt and the source template gamma's content share a token budget, so the effective prompt budget is smaller on large sources; prefer concise prompts where possible. prompt: string; // Advanced: Sharing and permissions configuration. Only use if user explicitly requests specific sharing settings. sharingOptions?: { // Share via email to specific recipients emailOptions?: { // Access level for email recipients access: "edit" | "comment" | "view" | "fullAccess"; // Email addresses to share with recipients: Array<string>; }; // Access level for external users externalAccess?: "edit" | "comment" | "view" | "noAccess"; // Access level for workspace members workspaceAccess?: "edit" | "comment" | "view" | "noAccess" | "fullAccess"; }; // Theme ID to use for the generated gamma. Only include when the user explicitly requests a theme change, or describes a desired visual style (e.g., “stylish,” “professional,” “cute,” “colorful,” “modern”). When omitted, the template’s theme applies. Call get_themes to look up available theme IDs, and evaluate each theme’s tone and color keywords against both the user’s aesthetic preference and the intent of the prompt to find the best match. themeId?: string; // Custom title for the generated Gamma (1–500 characters). Only include if the user explicitly provides or asks for a specific title; otherwise omit and a title will be derived from the content. title?: string; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ // Credit usage information credits?: { // Credits deducted for this generation deducted: number; // Remaining credits after generation remaining: number; }; // Error message (when status is failed) error?: string; // URL to download export file (when exportAs specified) exportUrl?: string; // URL to view and edit the Gamma in the Gamma editor. Share this with the user so they can customize the design, theme, layout, and content directly in Gamma. gammaUrl?: string; // Unique ID for the generation generationId: string; // Per-page results for a multi-page generation, in page order. Present once a multi-page generation completes; absent for single-page generations. Check each entry's status: if any page failed, tell the user which page(s) failed and why, including the failed page's gammaUrl so they can inspect it. When every page succeeded, do not relay per-page URLs — the top-level gammaUrl already reaches all pages, so listing each one is redundant. pages?: Array<{ // Error message if this page failed error?: string; // URL to download the exported file for this page (when exportAs specified) exportUrl?: string; // Doc ID of this page within the Gamma gammaId: string; // Direct URL to view and edit this page in the Gamma editor gammaUrl: string; // This page's generation status status: "pending" | "completed" | "failed"; }>; // Generation status status: "pending" | "completed" | "failed"; // Non-fatal warnings from the API when parts of the request were ignored or adjusted (e.g., imageOptions supplied on a non-AI template; sharing options stripped due to workspace restrictions). If present, relay to the user so they know which parameters did not take effect. warnings?: string; }>>; }; ```
427gamma_generate_imagegammawritecreativeCreate presentations and docs Generates one standalone image from a text prompt. Use this when the user wants an image, illustration, or photo on its own — NOT a presentation, document, or webpage (use generate for those), and NOT a file export of an existing Gamma (use export_gamma). Choose a type ("illustration", "scene", "photo", "abstract") and sizePreset for aspect ratio; for brand styling, find a themeId with get_themes, or omit it for the workspace default. Generation is asynchronous (it takes longer than a request can stay open): this returns immediately with an imageGenerationId and status "pending". If your host displays the image widget, it shows generation progress and the finished image on its own — do nothing else. If you do NOT have a widget UI (for example a CLI or terminal client), poll get_image_generation_status with that id, waiting a few seconds between checks (do not tight-loop), until status is "completed" (then share the returned image URL) or "failed" (then report the error). Do NOT call generate_image again to check progress (that starts a new, separately billed generation). This tool is part of plugin `Gamma`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gamma_generate_image(args: { // Description of the image to generate. Put background treatments here too (e.g. "on a white background", "contained in a circle"). prompt: string; // Up to 4 reference images whose subject (a character or product) should appear in the generated image. Only pass URLs the user supplied. referenceImages?: Array<{ // How the reference is used. Only "subject" is supported. role?: "subject"; // HTTPS URL of the reference image (subject to place in the scene). url: string; }>; // Aspect ratio of the output: "social-square" (1:1, default), "social-portrait" (4:5), "story" (9:16), "banner" (16:9), or "slide" (16:9). Exact pixel dimensions are chosen by the model. sizePreset?: "social-square" | "social-portrait" | "story" | "banner" | "slide"; // Theme to brand the images with. Use get_themes to find a themeId; omit to use the workspace default theme. Ignored when referenceImages are provided. themeId?: string; // Visual style: "illustration" (default), "scene" (narrative illustration), "photo" (photorealistic), or "abstract". Omit to use illustration. Ignored when referenceImages are provided — the references drive the look. type?: "illustration" | "scene" | "photo" | "abstract"; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; }; ```
428gamma_generate_multi_page_gammagammasensitive-writecreativeCreate presentations and docs Use this for one-shot creation of a MULTI-PAGE Gamma: a single Gamma containing several distinct pages under one URL. Ideal for sales rooms, proposal sites, onboarding portals, and microsites assembled from multiple sections (e.g. one page per prospect topic). Provide pages[] in the order they should appear; each page carries its own inputText and per-page settings (title, numCards, format, textMode, cardSplit, textOptions, imageOptions, path). File-wide settings (theme, folders, card dimensions, sharing, export, publish, overall title) apply to all pages. Prefer the generate tool when the user wants a single presentation, document, webpage, or social post; use this only when the user wants several distinct pages within one Gamma. This tool can only create new content — it cannot edit, modify, or refine an existing Gamma (including one it previously generated). After generation, direct the user to open their Gamma via the gammaUrl to make any edits, theme changes, or refinements in the Gamma editor. Do not offer to adjust, tweak, or refine the generated content yourself. Only include optional parameters when the user explicitly requests or clearly implies them. Gamma has intelligent defaults. When in doubt, omit. When uncertain about user preferences, ask rather than assume. Always share the output gammaUrl with the user when it's available. 429gamma_get_export_statusgammasensitive-writecreativeCreate presentations and docs Checks the status of an export previously started with export_gamma, using its exportId. Where an interactive widget is displayed, the widget polls for completion and shows the download link automatically, so only use this tool if the user explicitly asks for status. Where there is no interactive widget, such as a CLI or terminal client that does not render MCP Apps, poll this tool with the exportId until the status is "completed" or "failed". If the status is "pending", wait a few seconds before checking again; do not tight-loop. Returns "completed" with a download URL, "failed" with an error or reason, or "pending" if it is still rendering. On completion, share the download URL; on failure, report the error or reason. The download URL expires after about one week and is not tied to the API key, so share it carefully and download promptly. This tool is part of plugin `Gamma`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gamma_get_export_status(args: { // The export ID to check status for (returned by export_gamma). exportId: string; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; }; ```

433gamma_get_gamma_commentsgammawritecreativeCreate presentations and docs Lists comment threads on an existing Gamma presentation or document, including their replies. Use this when the user wants to read, review, or summarize the comments or feedback on a Gamma. Requires the Gamma file ID or URL. Results are paginated, oldest activity first; use `after` with the `nextCursor` from a previous response to fetch the next page. Use `updatedSince` (ISO-8601 timestamp) to fetch only threads with activity after a given time. 434gamma_get_gamma_viewer_analyticsgammasensitive-writecreativeCreate presentations and docs Gets the list of people who viewed an existing Gamma: display name and email for signed-in viewers (null for anonymous viewers), when they last opened it, and how many cards they viewed. Use this when the user asks who has seen a gamma, or to find a specific viewer by name or email. Results are paginated: use limit and the after cursor from the previous response to fetch more. To find a specific person (e.g. "get me the analytics for John Doe on this gamma"): scan each page for their name or email. Only conclude the person has not viewed the gamma after the last page (no nextCursor) — never from the first page alone. Once found, pass their viewerId as userId to get_gamma_viewer_detail_analytics for that person's detailed engagement. Requires at least edit permission on the gamma: manage permission shows all viewers, edit-only shows at most the API user's own activity. If the API returns a 403, tell the user analytics requires at least edit access on the gamma. Requires the Gamma file ID or URL. Analytics data is eventually consistent and can lag by about an hour. This tool is part of plugin `Gamma`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gamma_get_gamma_viewer_analytics(args: { // Cursor from a previous response to fetch the next page (optional) after?: string; // The Gamma file ID or a full Gamma URL. 435gamma_get_gamma_viewer_detail_analyticsgammawritecreativeCreate presentations and docs Gets one viewer's detailed engagement with an existing Gamma: their name and email, when they last opened it, how many of its cards they viewed, and the share of their total view time spent on each card. Every card in the gamma is included in deck order, each with its title (cardName, null for untitled cards) and 1-based position; cards the viewer never viewed have a viewTimePercent of 0. Refer to cards by title when available, falling back to "Card N". Use this when the user asks how a specific person engaged with a gamma. Requires the userId — the viewerId returned by get_gamma_viewer_analytics. If you only have a name or email, find the person with get_gamma_viewer_analytics first (paginating with the after cursor until found or pages run out). Anonymous viewers and users who did not view the gamma will not have valid analytics to find (404). Requires the Gamma file ID or URL. Analytics data is eventually consistent and can lag by about an hour. 485github_get_repogithubreadengineeringAccess repositories, issues, and pull requests. Required for some features such as Codex Retrieve metadata for a GitHub repository. You must populate exactly one of `repository_full_name`, `repository_id`, or `repository_url`: - `repository_full_name`: `owner/name`, such as `openai/openai`. Maps to GitHub REST `owner` and `repo` path parameters. - `repository_id`: numeric GitHub repository ID, such as `1296269`. - `repository_url`: repository URL or nested repository URL, such as a PR, issue, branch, file, REST API, GitHub Enterprise Server `/api/v3`, or GHE.com API URL. GitHub REST repository docs: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos#get-a-repository GitHub Enterprise Server REST docs: https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-server@latest/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api GHE.com API host docs: https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/data-residency/about-github-enterprise-cloud-with-data-residency#api-access. This tool is part of plugins `Codex Security`, `Data Analytics`, `GitHub`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__github_get_repo(args: { // Repository in `owner/name` form, such as `openai/openai`. This maps to GitHub REST `owner` and `repo` path parameters: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos#get-a-repository repository_full_name?: string | null; // Numeric GitHub repository ID, such as `1296269`. Use this only when the stable repository `id` from a GitHub repository object is available: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos#get-a-repository repository_id?: number | null; // GitHub repository URL, or a nested repository URL such as a pull request, issue, branch, or file URL. Examples: `https://github.com/openai/openai/pulls/123`, `https://api.github.com/repos/openai/openai`, `https://github.example.com/api/v3/repos/octo/repo`. Supports GitHub Enterprise Server custom hostnames and GHE.com API hosts. Docs: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/repos#get-a-repository and https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-server@latest/rest/using-the-rest-api/getting-started-with-the-rest-api and https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/admin/data-residency/about-github-enterprise-cloud-with-data-residency#api-access repository_url?: string | null; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ result: { [key: string]: unknown; }; }>>; }; ```

531gmail_apply_labels_to_emailsgmaildestructiveproductivityGmail tools for label counts, searching and reading emails/threads/attachments, reviewing drafts, and explicit mail changes like send, draft, forward, archive, Trash, and label actions. Apply labels to Gmail messages using label names rather than Gmail label IDs. This is the preferred labeling action for models because it avoids a separate label-id lookup step. Prefer this when the user refers to labels by name. This tool is part of plugins `Data Analytics`, `Gmail`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gmail_apply_labels_to_emails(args: { // Gmail label display names. This action accepts names and can create missing labels when create_missing_labels is true; batch_modify_email requires existing Gmail label IDs. add_label_names?: Array<string> | null; // Whether to create missing labels before applying them. create_missing_labels?: boolean; // Gmail message IDs returned by Gmail search/read results. Use `message_ids` from search_email_ids or `id` fields from email results. Do not pass placeholder values like `dummy`, `latest`, `gmail:<id>`, draft IDs, thread IDs, email addresses, subjects, or Gmail UI URLs. message_ids: Array<string>; // Gmail label display names. This action accepts names and can create missing labels when create_missing_labels is true; batch_modify_email requires existing Gmail label IDs. remove_label_names?: Array<string> | null; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ result: unknown; }>>; }; ```
532gmail_archive_emailsgmaildestructiveproductivityGmail tools for label counts, searching and reading emails/threads/attachments, reviewing drafts, and explicit mail changes like send, draft, forward, archive, Trash, and label actions. Archive Gmail threads while keeping their messages available in Gmail. The INBOX label is removed from every message currently in each thread, so the thread disappears from the inbox. 533gmail_batch_modify_emailgmaildestructiveproductivityGmail tools for label counts, searching and reading emails/threads/attachments, reviewing drafts, and explicit mail changes like send, draft, forward, archive, Trash, and label actions. Add or remove Gmail labels on a batch of individual messages. This modifies messages, not whole threads. To label by subject, sender, or search query, search first or use bulk_label_matching_emails/apply_labels_to_emails. This tool is part of plugins `Data Analytics`, `Gmail`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gmail_batch_modify_email(args: { // Existing Gmail label IDs to add, not label display names. Mutable system label IDs include INBOX, UNREAD, STARRED, IMPORTANT, SPAM, TRASH, and the CATEGORY_* labels. Gmail assigns SENT and DRAFT; they cannot be added or removed. For user labels, copy list_labels.labels[].id. Prefer apply_labels_to_emails when you have label names or want missing labels created. Do not pass search operators such as -in:trash, ALL, or display names. add_labels?: Array<string> | null; // Gmail message IDs returned by Gmail search/read results. Use `message_ids` from search_email_ids or `id` fields from email results. Do not pass placeholder values like `dummy`, `latest`, `gmail:<id>`, draft IDs, thread IDs, email addresses, subjects, or Gmail UI URLs. message_ids: Array<string>; // Existing Gmail label IDs to remove, not label display names. Mutable system label IDs include INBOX, UNREAD, STARRED, IMPORTANT, SPAM, TRASH, and the CATEGORY_* labels. Gmail assigns SENT and DRAFT; they cannot be added or removed. For user labels, copy list_labels.labels[].id. Prefer apply_labels_to_emails when you have label names. Do not pass search operators such as -in:trash, ALL, or display names. remove_labels?: Array<string> | null; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ result: unknown; }>>; }; ```

535gmail_batch_read_email_threadsgmaildestructiveproductivityGmail tools for label counts, searching and reading emails/threads/attachments, reviewing drafts, and explicit mail changes like send, draft, forward, archive, Trash, and label actions. Read recent messages from threads identified by message IDs or thread IDs. Supply at least one non-empty `message_ids` or `thread_ids` list; `message_ids` take precedence when both are supplied. Exact duplicate input IDs and duplicate resolved thread IDs are coalesced, preserving the first occurrence. Each thread contains at most `max_messages` messages, ordered from oldest to newest. Later IDs are ignored. The action fails if the combined serialized response exceeds 100 MB. This tool is part of plugins `Data Analytics`, `Gmail`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gmail_batch_read_email_threads(args: { // Optional maximum number of messages to include per thread; defaults to 20. max_messages?: number; // Gmail message IDs whose conversations should be read. Supply message_ids or thread_ids; message_ids take precedence when both are supplied. At most 100 are read. message_ids?: Array<string> | null; // Gmail thread IDs to read directly. Supply message_ids or thread_ids; message_ids take precedence when both are supplied. At most 100 are read. thread_ids?: Array<string> | null; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ result: unknown; }>>; }; ```

544gmail_read_attachmentgmaildestructiveproductivityGmail tools for label counts, searching and reading emails/threads/attachments, reviewing drafts, and explicit mail changes like send, draft, forward, archive, Trash, and label actions. Read one attachment from a Gmail message. First read/search the parent message and select an entry from its attachments, inline_images, or API-content MIME parts. For an attachments entry or downloadable MIME part, call this action only when its read_attachment_supported field is true; when false, do not call this action because the MIME type is unsupported. Pass the parent message id as message_id. Prefer the entry's non-null attachment_id or MIME part's body.attachment_id when its complete value is available; when it is absent or marked truncated, pass the exact filename instead. Do not synthesize attachment IDs from filenames, content IDs, x-attachment IDs, URLs, or user text. This tool is part of plugins `Data Analytics`, `Gmail`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gmail_read_attachment(args: { // Exact Gmail attachment_id copied from the selected attachment's attachments[].attachment_id or inline_images[].attachment_id, or from a downloadable API-content MIME part's body.attachment_id. Use it only when the complete value is available; if it is absent or marked truncated in a tool response, pass the exact filename instead. Do not pass truncated values, filenames, message IDs, thread IDs, Content-ID, X-Attachment-Id, URLs, or guessed values. attachment_id?: string; // Exact attachment filename from the parent message's attachments, inline_images, or API-content MIME parts. Do not pass extra parameters. id?: string | null; // Replies to add to existing Drive comment threads. Include all intended resolutions for this file in one call. resolutions?: Array<{ // Drive comment thread ID on the file. comment_id: string; // Optional reply text to include while resolving the comment. 592google_drive_searchgooglewriteproductivitySearch and work with files from Google Drive, Docs, Sheets, and Slides. Search Google Drive and return file or folder metadata. Calls without `item_type` and `page_token` retain the legacy search and optional best-effort text hydration. An explicit `image`, `document`, or `folder` item type searches exactly one metadata-only provider page; it never fetches file contents, even with `best_effort_fetch=True`. Return the opaque, provider-owned `next_page_token` unchanged as the next request's `page_token`. Use short, specific keywords, or omit the query to browse accessible files. Broaden an empty-result search with related terms, abbreviations, or synonyms. `special_filter_query_str` is a raw Google Drive v3 `q` filter for MIME type, modification time, ownership, sharing, or folder selection. Set `require_viewed_by_user=True` to restrict results to viewed files. Search covers all accessible drives by default. Do not pass unsupported `top_k`, `max_results`, `page_size`, `folder_url`, `query_type`, `user_message`, `recency_days`, `driveId`, or `include_shared_drives` fields. This tool is part of plugins `Data Analytics`, `Google Drive`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__google_drive_search(args: { // When true, attempt to fetch text content for each result. best_effort_fetch?: boolean; // Best-effort fetch timeout in seconds when best_effort_fetch=true. fetch_ttl?: number; // Restrict a paginated search to images, documents, or folders. item_type?: "image" | "document" | "folder" | null; // Opaque next_page_token returned by a previous Drive search. page_token?: string | null; // Optional keyword query for Drive search. Use concise terms like project/file names, or omit the query to browse accessible files. query?: string; // When true, keep only files viewed by the authenticated user. require_viewed_by_user?: boolean; // Optional raw Google Drive API `q` filter expression for advanced filtering. special_filter_query_str?: string; // Maximum results to return. Parameter name is `topn` (not `top_k`, `max_results`, or `page_size`). topn?: number; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ result: unknown; }>>; }; ```

This tool is part of plugins `Data Analytics`, `Google Drive`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__google_drive_update_file(args: { // Optional Google Drive API `addParents` query parameter: comma-separated parent folder IDs to add. Leave null for a metadata-only rename or move. Do not pass raw local file paths or string URLs. This parameter expects an absolute local file path. If you want to upload a file, provide the absolute path to that file here. file_uri?: string; // Optional MIME type for the replacement bytes. 602gsc_wizard_add_sitegscsensitive-writegrowthGoogle Search data analysis Registers a GSC property the user already has access to (in Google Search Console) inside GSC Wizard. The property URL must appear in Search Console — it is not provisioned by this call. Pass a URL prefix (https://example.com/) or a domain property (sc-domain:example.com). This tool is part of plugin `GSC Wizard`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gsc_wizard_add_site(args: { siteUrl: string; tags?: Array<string>; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ site?: { connectedAt?: unknown; id?: string | null; permissionLevel?: unknown; siteUrl?: unknown; tags?: Array<string> | null; }; }>>; }; ```
603gsc_wizard_add_tracked_urlsgscwritegrowthGoogle Search data analysis Adds URLs to the GSC Wizard Indexing Tracker for a property, creating the tracker if it does not exist yet. Each URL must belong to the property's domain. Enforces the 1,800-URL-per-tracker cap (URLs over the cap are skipped and reported). Newly added URLs start as "pending"; call check_tracked_url_now to inspect them immediately, or wait for the app's hourly cron. This tool is part of plugin `GSC Wizard`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gsc_wizard_add_tracked_urls(args: { siteUrl: string; urls: Array<string>; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ added?: unknown; alreadyTracked?: unknown; capacityRemaining?: unknown; requested?: number | null; siteUrl?: string | null; skippedOverCap?: unknown; trackerId?: unknown; }>>; }; ```
604gsc_wizard_analyze_cannibalizationgscreadgrowthGoogle Search data analysis Finds queries where multiple pages of the property compete for the same search, ranked by a cannibalization score (Shannon entropy over the pages’ impressions — higher means impressions split more evenly across pages, i.e. worse cannibalization). Served from the GSC Wizard ClickHouse warehouse when available, otherwise the live Search Console API (see `dataSource`). Date range is optional: omit startDate/endDate to analyze the last 28 settled days (data lags ~2-3 days). This tool is part of plugin `GSC Wizard`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gsc_wizard_analyze_cannibalization(args: { // Optional. Window end as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-31). You do NOT need to know today's date or the latest available date: omit this and the server uses the latest settled Search Console date (data lags ~2-3 days behind today). Never pass null or the string "null". endDate?: string; limit?: number; minImpressions?: number; searchType?: "web" | "image" | "video" | "news"; siteUrl: string; // Optional. Window start as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-03). You do NOT need to know today's date. Omit BOTH startDate and endDate to analyze the last 28 settled days automatically (Search Console data lags ~2-3 days). Never pass null or the string "null". startDate?: string; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ cannibalized?: Array<{ entropy?: unknown; pageCount?: unknown; pages?: Array<{ clicks?: unknown; ctr?: unknown; impressions?: unknown; position?: unknown; url?: unknown; }>; query?: unknown; totalClicks?: unknown; totalImpressions?: unknown; }>; dataSource?: unknown; minImpressions?: unknown; note?: unknown; range?: { days?: number | null; endDate?: unknown; startDate?: unknown; } | null; settledThrough?: unknown; siteUrl?: string | null; }>>; }; ```
605gsc_wizard_analyze_ctr_curvegscwritegrowthGoogle Search data analysis Builds the property’s actual click-through-rate curve bucketed by average position (1-20) and compares each bucket to one or more industry benchmarks. Available sources: awr (Advanced Web Ranking 2026), firstPageSage (First Page Sage 2026), sistrix (Sistrix 2024), backlinko (Backlinko 2019), or "all" (default) to compare against every source at once. Each bucket reports a `benchmarks` map (expected CTR per source) and a `deltas` map (actual minus expected; negative = underperforming); when a single source is selected the bucket also carries flat `expectedCtr`/`ctrDelta`. CTR values are 0-1 ratios. Served from the GSC Wizard ClickHouse warehouse when available, otherwise the live Search Console API (see `dataSource`). Date range is optional: omit startDate/endDate to analyze the last 28 settled days (data lags ~2-3 days). This tool is part of plugin `GSC Wizard`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gsc_wizard_analyze_ctr_curve(args: { benchmarkSource?: "awr" | "firstPageSage" | "sistrix" | "backlinko" | "all"; // Optional. Window end as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-31). You do NOT need to know today's date or the latest available date: omit this and the server uses the latest settled Search Console date (data lags ~2-3 days behind today). Never pass null or the string "null". endDate?: string; minImpressions?: number; searchType?: "web" | "image" | "video" | "news"; siteUrl: string; // Optional. Window start as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-03). You do NOT need to know today's date. Omit BOTH startDate and endDate to analyze the last 28 settled days automatically (Search Console data lags ~2-3 days). Never pass null or the string "null". startDate?: string; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ benchmarkSource?: unknown; buckets?: Array<{ benchmarks?: unknown; clicks?: unknown; ctr?: unknown; ctrDelta?: unknown; deltas?: unknown; expectedCtr?: unknown; impressions?: unknown; position?: unknown; queryCount?: unknown; }>; dataSource?: unknown; minImpressions?: unknown; note?: unknown; range?: { days?: number | null; endDate?: unknown; startDate?: unknown; } | null; settledThrough?: unknown; siteUrl?: string | null; sources?: Array<{ key?: unknown; label?: unknown; year?: unknown; }>; }>>; }; ```
606gsc_wizard_analyze_sampling_impactgscreadgrowthGoogle Search data analysis Estimates how much click/impression data Google Search Console hides through anonymization (privacy-threshold row dropping) for a property over a date range. Compares the per-day totals against the summed top query rows and top page rows; the gap is the lost share. On the live API path this reveals true GSC sampling. On the ClickHouse warehouse path the data is unsampled, so the reported loss reflects only top-N row truncation (see the `note` field). The response `dataSource` says which path served the request. Date range is optional: omit startDate/endDate to analyze the last 28 settled days (data lags ~2-3 days). This tool is part of plugin `GSC Wizard`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gsc_wizard_analyze_sampling_impact(args: { // Optional. Window end as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-31). You do NOT need to know today's date or the latest available date: omit this and the server uses the latest settled Search Console date (data lags ~2-3 days behind today). Never pass null or the string "null". endDate?: string; searchType?: "web" | "image" | "video" | "news"; siteUrl: string; // Optional. Window start as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-03). You do NOT need to know today's date. Omit BOTH startDate and endDate to analyze the last 28 settled days automatically (Search Console data lags ~2-3 days). Never pass null or the string "null". startDate?: string; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ dataSource?: unknown; note?: unknown; pageSampling?: { missingClicksPercent?: unknown; missingImpressionsPercent?: unknown; rowCount?: unknown; } | null; querySampling?: { missingClicksPercent?: unknown; missingImpressionsPercent?: unknown; rowCount?: unknown; } | null; range?: { days?: number | null; endDate?: unknown; startDate?: unknown; } | null; settledThrough?: unknown; siteUrl?: string | null; totals?: { clicks?: unknown; impressions?: unknown; } | null; }>>; }; ```
607gsc_wizard_audit_onpage_seogscreadgrowthGoogle Search data analysis Crawls a property's pages and runs a technical on-page/SEO audit per URL (Screaming-Frog style): HTTP status, indexability (noindex / canonicalised), title & meta-description length, H1s, word count, canonical, internal/external links, image alt coverage, structured data, Open Graph, viewport, hreflang, and a scored list of issues by severity. Pass explicit `urls`, or omit them to audit the top pages by Search Console impressions. URLs must belong to the property. Fetches each page live, so keep the count modest. 608gsc_wizard_breakdown_by_pathgscreadgrowthGoogle Search data analysis Aggregates page-level performance into a subdomain and first-folder breakdown. Each page URL is parsed and grouped by its host plus the first `depth` path segments (depth 1 -> /folder, depth 2 -> /folder/subfolder, etc.). Never pass null or the string "null". endDate?: string; limit?: number; searchType?: "web" | "image" | "video" | "news"; siteUrl: string; // Optional. Window start as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-03). You do NOT need to know today's date. Omit BOTH startDate and endDate to analyze the last 28 settled days automatically (Search Console data lags ~2-3 days). Never pass null or the string "null". startDate?: string; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ dataSource?: unknown; depth?: unknown; groups?: Array<{ avgPosition?: unknown; clicks?: unknown; ctr?: unknown; host?: unknown; impressions?: unknown; pageCount?: unknown; path?: unknown; subdomain?: unknown; }>; note?: unknown; range?: { days?: number | null; endDate?: unknown; startDate?: unknown; } | null; settledThrough?: unknown; siteUrl?: string | null; }>>; }; ```
609gsc_wizard_bulk_inspect_urlsgscreadgrowthGoogle Search data analysis Runs the Google URL Inspection API against a list of URLs serially, persisting each result to GSC Wizard's inspection history. Google caps inspections at 2,000 per property per day (shared across the UI and every MCP call); this tool counts each inspection against that cap and stops once it is reached, returning the URLs it could not get to. Call get_inspection_quota first if you want to see remaining headroom. Sequential to avoid hitting the per-second quota. This tool is part of plugin `GSC Wizard`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gsc_wizard_bulk_inspect_urls(args: { siteUrl: string; urls: Array<string>; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ count?: number | null; failed?: unknown; message?: unknown; quota?: { count?: unknown; limit?: unknown; remaining?: unknown; } | null; quotaExhausted?: boolean | null; results?: Array<{ coverageState?: unknown; error?: unknown; indexingState?: unknown; lastCrawlTime?: unknown; skipped?: unknown; url?: unknown; verdict?: unknown; }>; siteUrl?: string | null; skipped?: unknown; succeeded?: unknown; }>>; }; ```
610gsc_wizard_check_tracked_url_nowgscreadgrowthGoogle Search data analysis Triggers an immediate Google URL Inspection for up to 10 tracked URLs in the GSC Wizard Indexing Tracker, updating each URL's status, warnings, and append-only history. Counts against the daily 2,000-inspection/property quota — if the quota is exhausted the call returns a quota message instead of running. Use sparingly; the app's hourly cron checks tracked URLs automatically. This is a server-side write and is audit-logged. This tool is part of plugin `GSC Wizard`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gsc_wizard_check_tracked_url_now(args: { siteUrl: string; urls: Array<string>; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ count?: number | null; message?: unknown; quotaExhausted?: boolean | null; results?: Array<{ coverageState?: unknown; currentStatus?: unknown; error?: unknown; lastCrawlTime?: unknown; previousStatus?: unknown; url?: unknown; verdict?: unknown; warningType?: unknown; }>; siteUrl?: string | null; }>>; }; ```
611gsc_wizard_compare_migrationgscwritegrowthGoogle Search data analysis Before/after Search Console comparison for a site migration or restructure. Three modes: "cross-property" compares two GSC properties (old domain vs new); "two-urls" compares two URL-prefix sections within one property; "regex" splits one property by two regexes. Returns the daily clicks/impressions trend for each side, per-side totals, and the query and page winners/losers by click delta. Both sides use the same date window (this is A-vs-B, not two time periods). Reads the ClickHouse warehouse when available, else the live Search Console API. Date range is optional: omit startDate/endDate to analyze the last 28 settled days (data lags ~2-3 days). This tool is part of plugin `GSC Wizard`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gsc_wizard_compare_migration(args: { // Optional. You do NOT need to know today's date or the latest available date: omit this and the server uses the latest settled Search Console date (data lags ~2-3 days behind today). Never pass null or the string "null". endDate?: string; // Max query/page winners and losers to return per list (default 50). limit?: number; // cross-property | two-urls | regex. mode: "cross-property" | "two-urls" | "regex"; // Side A page regex (required for regex mode). regexA?: string; // Side B page regex (required for regex mode). regexB?: string; // Side A property (and the single property for two-urls/regex). siteUrl: string; // Side B property (required for cross-property). siteUrlB?: string; // Optional. Window start as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-03). You do NOT need to know today's date. Omit BOTH startDate and endDate to analyze the last 28 settled days automatically (Search Console data lags ~2-3 days). Never pass null or the string "null". startDate?: string; // Side A URL prefix (required for two-urls). urlPrefixA?: string; // Side B URL prefix (required for two-urls). urlPrefixB?: string; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ dailyTrend?: Array<unknown>; dataSource?: unknown; mode?: string | null; note?: unknown; pages?: unknown; queries?: unknown; range?: { days?: number | null; endDate?: unknown; startDate?: unknown; } | null; sides?: unknown; summary?: unknown; }>>; }; ```

624gsc_wizard_find_decaying_contentgscreadgrowthGoogle Search data analysis Finds queries or pages losing traffic between a baseline (earlier) period and a recent period, bucketed by severity of click loss (severe > 50%, moderate 20-50%, mild < 20%). Only keys with a meaningful baseline (clicks > 0 and impressions >= minImpressions) are considered. startDate/endDate is the RECENT period; comparisonStartDate/comparisonEndDate is the BASELINE period. For a full period-by-period matrix (clicks/impressions/position per month or week, like the app's Query Decay / Content Decay pages) use get_decay_overview instead. Served from the GSC Wizard ClickHouse warehouse when available, otherwise the live Search Console API (see `dataSource`). Date range is optional: omit startDate/endDate to analyze the last 28 settled days (data lags ~2-3 days). This tool is part of plugin `GSC Wizard`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gsc_wizard_find_decaying_content(args: { // Optional. End of the baseline / comparison period as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit both comparison dates to use the same-length period immediately before the current window. comparisonEndDate?: string; // Optional. Start of the baseline / comparison period as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit both comparison dates to use the same-length period immediately before the current window. comparisonStartDate?: string; dimension?: "query" | "page"; // Optional. Window end as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-31). You do NOT need to know today's date or the latest available date: omit this and the server uses the latest settled Search Console date (data lags ~2-3 days behind today). Never pass null or the string "null". endDate?: string; limit?: number; minImpressions?: number; searchType?: "web" | "image" | "video" | "news"; siteUrl: string; // Optional. Window start as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-03). You do NOT need to know today's date. Omit BOTH startDate and endDate to analyze the last 28 settled days automatically (Search Console data lags ~2-3 days). Never pass null or the string "null". startDate?: string; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ baseline?: unknown; counts?: { mild?: unknown; moderate?: unknown; severe?: unknown; } | null; dataSource?: unknown; decaying?: Array<{ baselineClicks?: unknown; baselineImpressions?: unknown; baselinePosition?: unknown; clickChangePct?: unknown; key?: unknown; positionDelta?: unknown; recentClicks?: unknown; recentImpressions?: unknown; recentPosition?: unknown; severity?: unknown; }>; dimension?: unknown; minImpressions?: unknown; note?: unknown; recent?: { days?: number | null; endDate?: unknown; startDate?: unknown; } | null; settledThrough?: unknown; siteUrl?: string | null; }>>; }; ```
625gsc_wizard_find_page_poaching_opportunitiesgscreadgrowthGoogle Search data analysis Finds queries ranking just outside the top positions (between minPosition and maxPosition) and estimates the click upside of pushing them to a target position. The upside is computed from the property's OWN CTR-by-position curve (derived from the same query data), not a broad industry benchmark, so the estimate reflects how this site actually converts impressions at that position. When the property has no data at the target position, falls back to the industry benchmark named by `fallbackBenchmark`: awr (Advanced Web Ranking 2026, default), firstPageSage (First Page Sage 2026), sistrix (Sistrix 2024), or backlinko (Backlinko 2019). The response reports `targetCtr` (the expected CTR used) and `ctrSource` ("own" or the benchmark key). Sorted by potential click gain. Served from the GSC Wizard ClickHouse warehouse when available, otherwise the live Search Console API (see `dataSource`). Date range is optional: omit startDate/endDate to analyze the last 28 settled days (data lags ~2-3 days). This tool is part of plugin `GSC Wizard`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gsc_wizard_find_page_poaching_opportunities(args: { // Optional. Window end as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-31). You do NOT need to know today's date or the latest available date: omit this and the server uses the latest settled Search Console date (data lags ~2-3 days behind today). Never pass null or the string "null". endDate?: string; fallbackBenchmark?: "awr" | "firstPageSage" | "sistrix" | "backlinko"; limit?: number; maxPosition?: number; minImpressions?: number; minPosition?: number; searchType?: "web" | "image" | "video" | "news"; siteUrl: string; // Optional. Window start as YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2026-05-03). You do NOT need to know today's date. Omit BOTH startDate and endDate to analyze the last 28 settled days automatically (Search Console data lags ~2-3 days). Never pass null or the string "null". startDate?: string; targetPosition?: number; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ ctrSource?: unknown; dataSource?: unknown; note?: unknown; opportunities?: Array<{ clicks?: unknown; ctr?: unknown; impressions?: unknown; position?: unknown; potentialClicks?: unknown; query?: unknown; }>; params?: unknown; range?: { days?: number | null; endDate?: unknown; startDate?: unknown; } | null; settledThrough?: unknown; siteUrl?: string | null; targetCtr?: unknown; }>>; }; ```
626gsc_wizard_forecast_trafficgscwritegrowthGoogle Search data analysis Projects future Search Console clicks (or impressions) for a property using the app's forecasting model: multiplicative seasonal decomposition (ratio-to-moving-average) plus an auto-selected trendline (linear / polynomial / log / exponential / power by best R-squared), re-seasonalised for each future period. Optionally applies a manual growth rate and derives revenue from a conversion rate and average order value. Reads the ClickHouse warehouse when available, else the live Search Console API. This tool is part of plugin `GSC Wizard`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__gsc_wizard_forecast_traffic(args: { // Optional flat sessions added to every forecast period. Default 0. additionalSessions?: number; // Optional average order value (in currency units) used with cvr for revenue. aov?: number; // Compound the growth rate across periods (default true). compoundGrowth?: boolean; // Currency label for the revenue fields (display only). currency?: string; // Optional conversion rate as a decimal (0.025 = 2.5%) to derive forecast revenue. cvr?: number; // How many future periods (weeks or months) to project. Default 26. forecastPeriods?: number; // Forecast granularity. Weekly needs >= 13 weeks of history, monthly >= 6 months. granularity?: "weekly" | "monthly"; // Optional manual growth rate per period as a decimal (0.05 = +5%). Default 0. growthRate?: number; // Trailing days of history to fit on (default 480 ≈ 16 months; more improves seasonality). historyDays?: number; // Metric to forecast (treated as "sessions" by the model). metric?: "clicks" | "impressions"; siteUrl: string; // Force a trendline model, or "auto" for the best R-squared (default). trendlineType?: "auto" | "linear" | "polynomial" | "logarithmic" | "exponential" | "power"; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ candidateTrendlines?: Array<{ r2?: unknown; type?: unknown; }>; currency?: unknown; dataSource?: unknown; forecast?: Array<{ baselineRevenue?: unknown; baselineSessions?: unknown; growthRevenue?: unknown; growthSessions?: unknown; period?: unknown; }>; granularity?: unknown; historicalPeriods?: unknown; historyRange?: { days?: number | null; endDate?: unknown; startDate?: unknown; } | null; metric?: unknown; note?: unknown; seasonalIndices?: Array<unknown>; settledThrough?: unknown; siteUrl?: string | null; trendline?: { equation?: unknown; r2?: unknown; type?: unknown; } | null; }>>; }; ```

721heygen_video_agent_generateheygenwritecreativeCreate AI videos The primary tool for video creation using HeyGen's Video Agent. Use this tool to generate videos on behalf of the user. ### WHEN TO CALL: - If the user explicitly requests this tool or mentions "HeyGen Video Agent", invoke it. - User provides a SPECIFIC topic AND narrative details, script, or style instructions (e.g., "Make a 30-second product demo for our AI scheduling app with a professional tone" or "Create a video explaining basketball rules with an energetic narrator"). - High-intent users: Specific topic + content/narrative/script provided. ### NEVER CALL WHEN: - The request is vague or lacks a specific topic (e.g., "Make me a video" or "Help me with a video about coding"). Instead, stay in chat and help the user define their topic, narrative, and style before calling this tool. ### SESSION MANAGEMENT: - First call: Leave session_id empty. A new session will be created automatically. - Subsequent calls (continuing a conversation): Pass the session_id returned from the previous tool call. This continues the conversation and keeps the agent in the loop. - New video request: If the user explicitly asks to start a completely new video, leave session_id empty to create a fresh session. ### INPUTS: - prompt: (Required) The user's direct request for the video. - conversation_context: (Optional) All relevant context from the conversation that informs this request. IMPORTANT: Always include the actual content being referenced—never use vague references like "the script above", "as mentioned", or "that idea". Expand all pronouns and references into the actual material. - session_id: (Optional) Session ID from a previous tool call to continue the conversation. This tool is part of plugin `HeyGen`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__heygen_video_agent_generate(args: { conversationContext?: string | null; prompt: string; sessionId?: string | null; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; }; ```
722hostinger_websites_createhostingerwriteotherBuild websites by chatting Create new Hostinger Horizons website from the given message.\n Use this tool when user asks you to create a website, landing page, blog or any other type of application.\n This tool initiates the website creation process and returns a website URL and ID. The generation happens asynchronously.\n After invoking this tool, your chat reply must be EXACTLY 1 sentence summarizing that Hostinger Horizons is now creating their website and it will be ready in a few minutes and you should provide the website URL to the user immediately Do not write code.\n\nTo edit afterwards, users must go to Hostinger Horizons interface in the provided website URL. If the tool call fails with an error, you should provide a clear explanation of the error and do not generate code yourself in the chat. \n TECHNOLOGY STACK CONSTRAINTS (STRICTLY ENFORCED):\n The environment is limited to the following technologies. You MUST NOT use, suggest, or implement any technology outside this list:\n \n - Language: JavaScript ONLY. - Languages like TypeScript, Rust, Python, Java, PHP, etc., are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.\n - Framework: React.\n - Navigation: React Router.\n - Styling: TailwindCSS.\n - Components: shadcn/ui (built with @radix-ui primitives).\n - Icons: Lucide React.\n - Animations: Framer Motion.\n \n BACKEND & DATA STORAGE:\n - Horizons integrated backend is the EXCLUSIVE solution for persistent data storage, authentication, and database needs.\n - Local databases (SQLite, MySQL, etc.) are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.\n - Third-party services (Firebase, AWS Amplify) are allowed ONLY if explicitly requested by the user.\n \n MAPS:\n - OpenStreetMap is the default provider.\n - Alternative providers (Google Maps, Mapbox) are allowed ONLY if explicitly requested by the user.\n. This tool is part of plugin `Hostinger`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__hostinger_websites_create(args: { message: Array<{ // Detailed project specification. // Include purpose, key features, user flows, data models, and design preferences. // The specification should be detailed and comprehensive, covering all aspects of the project. text: string; type: "text"; }>; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; }; ```

740ideomine_add_images_to_collectionideominewriteotherTools for working with iDeoMine. Add one or more images to an existing Ideogram collection. `collection_id` is the URL-safe base64 collection identifier returned by `list_collections` or `create_collection`. Pass at least one of: - `image_response_ids`: response_ids of AI-generated images. These appear as `response_id` in `get_images_by_collection_id` results and as the `response_ids` array in `structured_content` from generation tools. - `image_upload_ids`: upload ids of uploaded images. These appear as `image_id` in `get_images_by_collection_id` results and as the `id` field in `upload_image`'s curl response. Both lists may be combined. The response reports `added_count`, `failed_count`, and per-asset failure reasons. 745ideomine_edit_imageideominesensitive-writeotherTools for working with iDeoMine. Edit a previously generated or uploaded image using a text prompt. STRICT: "edit" means edit *this* image. This tool is NOT a remix, NOT a "generate something similar." If this tool fails or can't proceed for any reason, surface the failure to the user verbatim and stop. Do NOT fall back to `generate_image` or `remix_image` to produce a "similar" result — that is not what the user asked for. Pass at least one of: - `image_response_ids`: response_ids of images previously generated by `generate_image` / `generate_images_bulk`. They appear as the `response_ids` array in the previous tool's `structured_content`. One response_id per image. - `image_upload_ids`: upload ids returned by the `upload_image` curl response (the `id` field of that JSON, NOT the `image_url`). For a user who drag-and-dropped an image into the chat: call `upload_image` first to mint a one-shot URL, run its curl in the sandbox, then pass the returned `id` here. Both lists may be combined — every reference becomes an entry in the same edit-reference parent, and the model produces one new image conditioned on all of them. Returns a `running` envelope just like a fresh generation; the user asks for status the same way. Optionally pass a `collection_id` to save the edited image into an existing collection. `private`: omit to use the account's plan default (paid → private, free/Basic → public). Pass `False` only when the user explicitly asks to publish to the public Ideogram feed. Enterprise generations are always private regardless. If the user dropped an image and asked to edit it but `upload_image` / curl is unavailable (sandbox not allowed-listed, etc.), tell the user how to enable the upload (per `upload_image`'s sandbox hint) and stop. Do not invent an alternative. This tool is part of plugin `iDeoMine`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__ideomine_edit_image(args: { aspect_ratio?: string | null; collection_id?: string | null; image_response_ids?: Array<string> | null; image_upload_ids?: Array<string> | null; magic_prompt?: "AUTO" | "ON" | "OFF" | null; private?: boolean | null; prompt: string; seed?: number | null; }): Promise<CallToolResult>; }; ```
746ideomine_generate_imageideominesensitive-writeotherTools for working with iDeoMine. Generate one image from a text prompt using Ideogram's AI. Defaults to Ideogram 4.0 (the latest, highest-quality model) rendered at top quality. Just pass a `prompt` — the defaults are good; avoid over-specifying. Returns immediately with `{status: "running", request_id, ...}`. The widget renders spinners and auto-updates. In text-only clients, tell the user they can ask for a status update at any time — that calls `get_generation_status` and renders a session-wide status table. Use `generate_images_bulk` instead when the user wants several distinct prompts rendered in parallel (e.g. "5 variations of a sunset"). Parameter guidance: - resolution: optional exact pixel dimensions (e.g. `"2048x2048"`). When both `resolution` and `aspect_ratio` are given, `resolution` wins. Shorthand: "1k" → `"1024x1024"`, "2k" → `"2048x2048"`. - rendering_speed: controls the quality/speed trade-off on BOTH the default v4 model and custom (v3) models. v4 supports QUALITY, BALANCED, and FAST; a FLASH request on v4 is treated as FAST (v4 has no separate FLASH tier). - custom_model_uri: pass ONLY when the user wants to generate with their own custom/fine-tuned model. Custom models run on the v3 pipeline, which enables the knobs below. Omit it to use the default Ideogram 4.0 model. - style_type, negative_prompt, seed: these apply ONLY to a custom-model (v3) generation and are ignored on the default v4 path. Omit them unless the user is using a custom model and asks. - collection_id: optionally pass to save the finished image into an existing collection. - private: omit to use the account's plan default (paid → private, free/Basic → public). Pass `False` only when the user explicitly asks to publish to the public Ideogram feed. Enterprise generations are always private regardless.
