1374vidiq_vidiq_similar_channelsvidiqwritegrowthYouTube stats and keywords Find COMPETITORS of a channel — either the user's own channel or a specific named channel. Uses neural semantic search tuned for competitor matching; the user's own authorized channels are automatically excluded from results. Use this tool ONLY when someone asks for competitors or similar channels relative to a channel: - "Who are my competitors?" or "Find channels like mine" (the user's own channel — country/language are auto-detected from it) - "Channels similar to [channel]", "Competitors of [channel]", or "Channels like @handle" (a named reference channel — see SIMILAR TO A SPECIFIC CHANNEL below) Do NOT use this tool for generic channel discovery by topic, size, growth, or any other criteria ("find tech review channels", "top gaming channels in Brazil", "fastest growing fitness channels") — use vidiq_channel_search for that. The 'niche' parameter is required — always provide a clear topic or content theme. Optionally narrow results with minSubscribers and maxSubscribers. SIMILAR TO A SPECIFIC CHANNEL — when the user names a reference channel ("channels similar to Creator Insider", "competitors of MrBeast", "channels like @veritasium"), do NOT guess its characteristics. First resolve the channel with vidiq_channel_search (it returns channelId, niche, subNiches, subscriberCount, country, languages), then call this tool with: - niche: copied verbatim from the reference channel's niche + subNiches, comma-separated (e.g. 'YouTube Growth, Monetization & SEO') — do NOT invent your own niche wording when the channel was found; only fall back to your own description if the channel was not found or its niche is empty - country: the reference channel's country - language: the first code from the reference channel's languages - minSubscribers / maxSubscribers: a band around the reference channel's subscriberCount so results are in a similar league — roughly 10% of it as minSubscribers and 5x it as maxSubscribers (e.g. 300k subs → minSubscribers=30000, maxSubscribers=1500000), unless the user asks for a specific range - avgViews: the reference channel's avgViews (from vidiq_channel_search) — pass it so results are auto-ranged to a similar per-video-views league. Do NOT also set avgViewsMin/avgViewsMax unless the user asks for a specific average-views range. - excludeChannelIds: [the reference channel's channelId] — otherwise the channel appears in its own competitor list Skipping this step produces noticeably worse, off-vibe results. Results are ranked by neural similarity combining content overlap, audience size proximity, and niche alignment. Each result includes the channel's title, subscriber count, niches, languages, and country. Optionally filter by country (ISO 3166-1 two-letter code) and/or language (ISO 639-1 code). When not provided, these are auto-detected from the user's authorized channel. Cost: 5 credit(s) per call. This tool is part of plugin `vidIQ`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__vidiq_vidiq_similar_channels(args: { // The reference channel's lifetime average views per video (total views / total videos). When searching for competitors of a specific channel, pass its avgViews here so results are auto-ranged to a similar per-video-views league (parallels passing the reference channel's subscriber band). Leave unset for generic niche searches. avgViews?: number; // Manual upper bound for lifetime average views per video (total views / total videos), overriding the avgViews auto-range. Use together with avgViewsMin to define a specific per-video average-views range. avgViewsMax?: number; // Manual lower bound for lifetime average views per video (total views / total videos), overriding the avgViews auto-range. Use to require results that average at least this many views per video — e.g. 50000 for '50k+ average views'. This is the per-video average, not total views. avgViewsMin?: number; // Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code to filter results by channel country — e.g. 'US', 'GB', 'BR', 'JP'. When omitted, the country is auto-detected from the user's authorized channel (if any). country?: string; // Channel IDs to exclude from results. When searching for competitors of a specific named channel, ALWAYS pass that channel's channelId here so it does not appear in its own competitor list. The user's own authorized channels are excluded automatically and do not need to be listed. excludeChannelIds?: Array<string>; // Two-letter ISO 639-1 language code to filter results by channel language — e.g. 'en', 'es', 'pt', 'ja'. Only a single language is accepted. When omitted, the language is auto-detected from the user's authorized channel (if any). language?: string; // Upper bound for subscriber count. Use to filter out larger channels — e.g. 1000000 to cap results at channels under 1M subscribers. Use together with minSubscribers to define a specific range. maxSubscribers?: number; // Lower bound for subscriber count. Use to filter out smaller channels — e.g. 10000 to only see channels with 10k+ subscribers. Use together with maxSubscribers to define a specific range. minSubscribers?: number; // The niche, topic, or content theme to search for similar channels in. Use natural language — e.g. 'tech reviews', 'vegan cooking tutorials', 'Minecraft let's plays', 'personal finance for millennials'. This is the primary search query and must always be provided. niche: string; // Number of similar channels to return. Defaults to 30, maximum 50. size?: number; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ similarChannels: Array<{ avgViews: number | null; channelId: string; channelTitle: string; country: string | null; languages: string | null; niches: string; subscriberCount: number; }>; }>>; }; ```

1376vidiq_vidiq_similar_videosvidiqdestructivegrowthYouTube stats and keywords Find high-performing YouTube videos similar to a seed video - the video-level counterpart of vidiq_similar_channels. Give it one video ID or URL and it returns videos ranked by combined similarity: textual (title/topic) and visual (thumbnail), fused with each video labeled by which signals matched (`matchedBy`; matching both earns a ranking boost). Use this for topic ideation ('find 50 videos like this outlier'), studying how a proven concept is packaged across channels, or expanding one winning video into a content cluster. Searches vidIQ's high-performing/outlier video index - results skew toward videos that overperform, which is what makes them useful as ideation references. Results are ordered most-similar-first; no numeric similarity score is exposed. Use `minEngagementRate` to filter copycat/re-upload spam around viral seeds. Check `signalsUsed`/`signalsFailed` before interpreting an empty result. For channel-level similarity use vidiq_similar_channels; for thumbnail-only search use vidiq_similar_thumbnails. Cost: 5 credit(s) per call. This tool is part of plugin `vidIQ`. exec tool declaration: ```ts declare const tools: { mcp__codex_apps__vidiq_vidiq_similar_videos(args: { // Filter by channel country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. 'US') channelCountry?: string; // Filter results by format. Note: thumbnail similarity only covers long-form videos, so 'short' results come from title similarity alone. contentType?: "all" | "long" | "short"; // Set true to drop videos from the seed video's own channel. excludeSeedChannel?: boolean; // Number of results to return limit?: number; // Similarity signals to use. 'both' (default) fuses title/topic similarity with thumbnail visual similarity. 'title' uses only textual similarity (works for Shorts). 'thumbnail' uses only visual thumbnail similarity (long-form index only). matchOn?: "both" | "title" | "thumbnail"; // Maximum channel subscribers maxSubscribers?: number; // Maximum video views maxViews?: number; // Minimum engagement rate (likes/views, 0-1). Filters out low-engagement copycat/re-upload channels that flood results for viral seeds; real creators typically show 0.03-0.12, content farms 0.002-0.01. Recommended around 0.02 when seeding from a mega-viral video. minEngagementRate?: number; // Minimum channel subscribers minSubscribers?: number; // Minimum video views minViews?: number; // Filter by publish date publishedWithin?: "thisWeek" | "thisMonth" | "threeMonths" | "sixMonths" | "oneYear" | "allTime"; // Seed YouTube video: an 11-character video ID (e.g. 'dQw4w9WgXcQ') or a video URL. Results are videos similar to this one. videoId: string; }): Promise<CallToolResult<{ seed: { channelId: string; channelTitle: string; videoId: string; videoTitle: string; }; // Requested signals that could not run, with a stable public reason code. signalsFailed: Array<{ reason: "unsupported_content_type" | "seed_thumbnail_unavailable" | "service_unavailable"; signal: "title" | "thumbnail"; }>; // Signals whose search actually ran and contributed candidates. If a requested signal is missing here, its search did not run - do NOT conclude 'no similar videos exist' for that signal. signalsUsed: Array<"title" | "thumbnail">; videos: Array<{ breakoutScore: number; channelCountry: string | null; channelId: string; channelThumbnail: string | null; channelTitle: string | null; engagementRate: number | null; mainCategory: string | null; // Which similarity signals matched this video. Matching both earns a rank-fusion boost. matchedBy: Array<"title" | "thumbnail">; subscriberCount: number | null; trendCategories: Array<string> | null; videoDuration: number; videoId: string; videoPublishedAt: number; videoTags: Array<string>; videoThumbnail: string; videoTitle: string; videoTopics: Array<string>; videoType: string | null; viewCount: number; vph: number | null; }>; }>>; }; ```

1413vixnode_modify_web_pagevixnodewriteotherBuild websites with AI Modify an existing web page under a specific project and publish the latest HTML content. IMPORTANT: Before regenerating the page HTML for any modification, ALWAYS call get_project_page_html first to fetch the latest live HTML of the page. Never generate new HTML from memory or a stale copy; always base your changes on the freshly fetched HTML to avoid overwriting updates made after the last call. Target confirmation rule: if the user does not clearly specify the modification target (for example which project/page/section/content to update), the assistant MUST ask for confirmation first and must not modify proactively. Do not display project_id or page_id to the user unless the user explicitly asks for those IDs. Theme/style rule: only when the user asks to change style, theme, color palette, layout, visual tone, or overall look-and-feel, the assistant MUST first call get_reference_themes or show suitable themes. Modification flow: 1. Call get_project_page_html to read the current HTML. 2. If the modification is about content only, apply changes to the fetched HTML and call this tool for preview/confirmation. 3. If the modification is about style/theme/layout/look-and-feel: show or retrieve reference themes first; wait for the user to select a theme; ask whether to apply the selected theme; only after confirmation, generate HTML aligned to that theme and call this tool. 4. The page is modified only after user confirmation in the UI. If HTML is truncated and cannot be previewed correctly, ask the user to try ChatGPT Work mode: https://chatgpt.com/?surface=work. Important theme mapping rule: if the user selected a theme id such as Style-16, that theme id is only a reference used to derive the final HTML/CSS.
